plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: A fragrant evergreen shrub with silvery-gray foliage and dense spikes of small tubular flowers. It is widely cultivated in gardens and in commercial fields for essential oils, and its blooms attract bees and butterflies in great numbers.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late June to August in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to the Mediterranean; cultivated in Provence (France), England, Tasmania, and the northern United States
plants.funFact: The name Lavandula likely comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash', since the Romans used lavender to scent their baths.

plants.name: Hydrangea macrophylla
plants.description: A deciduous shrub producing large rounded clusters of showy flowers. It is a classic summer garden plant in temperate regions, and is popular in coastal areas and cottage gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early summer to early autumn (June to September)
plants.location: Native to Japan; widely grown in the UK, the eastern United States, the Azores, and New Zealand
plants.funFact: Flower color depends on soil pH: acidic soils with available aluminum yield blue blooms, while alkaline soils yield pink ones.

plants.name: Nymphaea alba
plants.description: An aquatic perennial with floating round leaves and large, fragrant, star-shaped flowers that open in the morning and close in the afternoon. It grows in lakes, ponds, and slow rivers.
plants.location: Lakes and ponds across Europe, North Africa, and parts of western Asia
plants.funFact: The flowers close and sink slightly underwater at night, then rise and reopen with the morning sun.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A striking evergreen shrub with the largest flower head in the Protea genus, composed of a central cone of tiny flowers surrounded by showy bracts. In the Southern Hemisphere it blooms in the cool season, as winter begins.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn through winter in the Southern Hemisphere; peak around May to September
plants.location: Fynbos regions of the Western and Eastern Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: It is the national flower of South Africa and can survive wildfires thanks to a woody underground rootstock that resprouts after burning.
